candidates.source_name: Pályázati Portál – Támogatott projektkereső (palyazat.gov.hu, supported-project search)
candidates.why_relevant: Central Hungarian register of every EU-cofinanced supported project (~529k records observed) with beneficiary name, project title, awarded amount, decision date, OP code and location; filterable by operative programme (GINOP/GINOP Plusz, DIMOP Plusz, KÖFOP) and applicant name, with an Export function. This is the primary way to enumerate funded digitalisation projects at banks, savings institutions, fintechs, payment/POS integrators and public financial IT bodies (Magyar Államkincstár, NAV) before or instead of a procurement notice.
candidates.source_subtype: government grant-beneficiary register / searchable database with export
candidates.access_status: public, no login observed; JS-driven search UI, export offered
candidates.legal_status: public sector information published under EU cohesion transparency obligations
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic filtered crawl/export by OP (GINOP, GINOP Plusz, DIMOP Plusz, KÖFOP, RRF) plus applicant-name queries for known banks/vendors; store beneficiary, amount, code, date; diff monthly. Check for an underlying JSON/XHR endpoint before HTML scraping.
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed query + direct fetch of results page to confirm fields

negative_findings.description: Neither the national supported-project search nor Kohesio offers a filter for 'financial sector' or 'payments'; the national search filters are programme, year, OP, call title, applicant name, fund and geography only.
negative_findings.result_summary: Sector targeting must be done by keyword on project titles/descriptions and by applicant-name lists of known banks, savings institutions, fintechs and POS/payment vendors, or via NACE codes on the state-aid side.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design must include a curated actor list and a Hungarian keyword lexicon rather than relying on a sector facet; recall will otherwise be poor.

negative_findings.description: Grant registers publish the beneficiary, not the supplier that implements the project. No source found in this cell exposes the implementing IT vendor for a privately funded grant project.
negative_findings.result_summary: Supplier identification requires joining grant records to public procurement (EKR/TED/Közbeszerzési Értesítő) for public beneficiaries, or to vendor case studies/press for private ones.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Cell #15 alone cannot answer 'who supplied it' for private beneficiaries; the workstream needs an explicit join step with the procurement cells.

negative_findings.description: No documented open API or bulk download endpoint was found for the palyazat.gov.hu supported-project search; only an in-page Export control was observed and its formats were not stated.
negative_findings.result_summary: Treat bulk extraction as unresolved; an XHR/JSON endpoint may exist behind the search UI but was not confirmed in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Affects feasibility and cost of systematic monitoring of the single most important source in this cell.

negative_findings.description: Searches did not surface a Hungarian national state-aid transparency portal separate from the Commission's TAM; secondary commentary indicates Hungary reports through TAM while some other Member States use domestic sites.
negative_findings.result_summary: This is unverified secondary commentary, not a confirmed fact about Hungary's reporting channel.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If a domestic Hungarian aid register (e.g. under the Támogatásokat Vizsgáló Iroda) exists, it would be an additional high-value source; needs a dedicated hu-language check.

negative_findings.description: Several local terms are noisy: 'DIMOP pályázat' and 'GINOP pályázat' return overwhelmingly SEO/consultancy marketing pages; 'digitalizáció' alone returns generic SME IT content unrelated to financial infrastructure; 'fizetés' collides with 'salary/payment of wages'.
negative_findings.result_summary: Query design should combine programme codes with financial terms (bank, hitelintézet, pénzforgalom, kártyaelfogadás, POS, terminál, számlavezetés) and exclude consultancy domains.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents precision collapse in automated collection.

coverage_gaps.description: Támogatásokat Vizsgáló Iroda (TVI, the Hungarian state aid monitoring office at the Ministry of Finance) and any national de minimis / aid register were not searched in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run hu queries for 'Támogatásokat Vizsgáló Iroda', 'állami támogatás nyilvántartás', 'de minimis nyilvántartás' and assess whether a national beneficiary register exists.

coverage_gaps.description: EU centrally-managed programmes that also fund financial/payment digitalisation in Hungary were out of the searched set: Digital Europe Programme, Horizon Europe, InvestEU / EIF guarantee intermediaries, and Interreg. Their beneficiary databases (CORDIS, Funding & Tenders portal, EIF intermediary lists) name Hungarian fintech and IT participants.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add CORDIS, the EU Funding & Tenders portal beneficiary search, and EIF/InvestEU Hungarian intermediary lists as a follow-up sweep.

coverage_gaps.description: Kohesio's Hungarian coverage for the 2021-2027 period is described as progressively backfilled; the actual completeness for GINOP Plusz / DIMOP Plusz records was not verified.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Download the HU dataset and compare record counts and latest decision dates against the national register to establish which source leads.

coverage_gaps.description: No verified crosswalk was established between grant project codes (e.g. DIMOP_Plusz-1.3.7-23-2023-00001) and company identifiers (adószám / cégjegyzékszám), which is needed to link beneficiaries to company registry and financial data.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Test whether project detail pages or the export include tax numbers; otherwise plan a name-matching layer against the Hungarian company registry (e-cegjegyzek / OPTEN / Bisnode).

coverage_gaps.description: Regional OPs (TOP Plusz) and county-level grant decisions that fund municipal digital service and e-payment projects were only glimpsed via one filtered URL and not systematically explored.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate TOP Plusz calls with digital/e-service content and their awarded projects, which often include municipal payment and card-acceptance components.

brief: Hungary's subsidy transparency layer is unusually rich for this cell: a single national register (palyazat.gov.hu Támogatott projektkereső, ~529k records, daily-updated from EMIR/EUPR/IIER, with an export function) plus EU-level mirrors (Kohesio, Cohesion Open Data, the State Aid Transparency Award Module) make beneficiaries, amounts and project scope of GINOP/GINOP Plusz, DIMOP Plusz, KÖFOP and RRF digitalisation projects systematically enumerable. The highest-leverage vendor source is the MKIK 'Vállalkozz digitálisan!' accredited supplier catalogue, because DIMOP Plusz SME digitalisation calls force purchases from it — effectively a state-maintained roster of eligible IT and payment-adjacent suppliers — complemented by MFB's published list of financial intermediaries that distribute the combined loan-plus-grant instruments, which doubles as a map of which banks sit in the EU-money channel. The structural weakness is that grant registers name the beneficiary and never the implementing supplier, so private-sector projects must be joined to procurement notices, vendor case studies or press to identify who actually built the system. Local-language search was essential and decisive here: the accreditation catalogue, the MFB intermediary requirement, the DIMOP managing authority site and the Treasury/NAV project disclosures surfaced only through Hungarian queries, while English queries reached the EU-level aggregators.
